court: In the High Court of Madras†
case_number: Crl. O.P. [MD] No. 19777 of 2018 and Crl. M.P.(MD) Nos. 9047 & 9048 of 2018
prayer: Prayer: Criminal Original Petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., to transfer the C.C. No. 15 of 2018 pending on the file of the Judicial Magistrate Fast Track Court at Magisterial Level, Thanjavur to the Judicial Magistrate Fast Track Court at Magisterial Level, Alandur, Kancheepuram District.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

N. Seshasayee, J.:— This petition is preferred by the husband of the accused in C.C. No. 15 of 2018 on the file of Judicial Magistrate No. I, Fast Track Court, Alandur, against the complaint laid by the respondent for an offence alleged to have been committed under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.

2. The case of the petitioner is that the respondent/complainant before the trial Court was running a chit business, that he had entrusted his blank cheques as security, that even though the entire chit transactions were concluded, the respondent instead of delivering back the cheques issued by him, has been misusing the same, and has been instituting cases against his wife and him under Sec. 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. In particular, he has instituted C.C. No. 53/2018 before the Judicial Magistrate No, I, (FTC) Alandur against his (the petitioner's) wife Anusiya and against him in CC. No. 15/2018 before the Judicial Magistrate (FTC) Thanjavur. He now requires transfer of the second mentioned case pending before the Judicial Magistrate (FTC) Thanjavur to the Judicial Magistrate (FTC) Alandur.

3. In his counter, the respondent has alleged that he is an insurance agent working for few Insurance Companies, that he had known the petitioner's wife for sometime, and when a request was made, he gave her a loan of Rs. 12 lakhs, that in partial repayment of the same, petitioner's wife had issued 2 cheques for a total amount of Rs. 9,75,000/-, that when he presented the cheques with his banker M/s. City Union Bank, Kottivakkam Branch, Chennai, the same came to be dishonoured on the ground that the payments of the same had been stopped by the drawer of the cheques. This led to the filing of C.C. No. 53/2018 against the petitioner's wife. The evidence on his side was concluded and the case was posted for questioning under Sec. 163 Cr.P.C.

4. So far as C.C. No. 15/2018 filed against the present petitioner before the Judicial Magistrate (FTC) Thanjavur is concerned, the petitioner had borrowed some amounts for his business purposes between 13.06.2016 and 05.07.2017, and towards repayment of the same, he had issued 3 crossed cheques for Rs. 4.50 lakhs each. When the respondent presented these cheques with its banker M/s. Indian Overseas Bank, Sengipatti Branch, Thanjavur District, they came to be dishonoured, on grounds of insufficiency of funds in the account of the petitioner. The cause of action in both the cases are different.

5. The arguments were advanced in line with the allegations made by the rival side as stated above.

6. This Court finds that merely because the complainant happens to be the same person in both the cases, that does not ipso facto imply that both the cases must be tried before the same Court especially when the cause of action for both the cases, one pending against the petitioner and the other pending against the petitioner's wife, are different. Secondly, the timing of the petition also does not enthuse this Court, since in C.C. No. 53/2018, pending against petitioner's wife, the complainant side evidence has concluded. This Court therefore does not consider it necessary to transfer C.C. No. 15/2018 pending before Judicial Magistrate (FTC) Thanjavur to Judicial Magistrate (FTC) Alandur.

7. There is yet another prayer and that pertains to seeking dispensation from personal appearance before the Judicial Magistrate Court at Thanjavur. The petitioner can move the learned Magistrate under Section 205 Cr.P.C, if he is so desirous and, if any such petition is filed the learned Magistrate may decide the same on merits.

8. Subject to the above observation, this criminal original petition is dismissed. Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
